name: Hot Pixel Detection
description: Detects hot/dead pixel patterns absent in AI images
algorithm: Hot Pixel Detection — Sensor/Physical Model Analyzer
mechanism:
This method analyzes physical camera/sensor characteristics:

1. **Sensor Model**: Expected sensor characteristics are modeled based on camera physics.

2. **Feature Extraction**: Detects hot/dead pixel patterns absent in AI images. Physical artifacts from real camera sensors are analyzed.

3. **Authenticity Check**: Presence or absence of expected sensor patterns is evaluated.

4. **AI Comparison**: Results are compared against known AI generation patterns.

5. **Confidence Score**: A score reflecting the likelihood of authentic sensor origin is computed.
parameters:
Analysis type: sensor
Media: image
Input: Raw pixel data / image file
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Processing: Client-side Canvas API
Color spaces: RGB, Grayscale as applicable
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-90% standalone accuracy. Performance is highest on uncompressed images and may decrease with heavy JPEG compression or social media re-encoding.
source: Digital image forensics research. Based on signal processing and computational photography principles.
useCase: Detection of AI-generated or manipulated images through hot pixel detection analysis. This method identifies patterns and artifacts that are characteristic of AI generation, contributing to a comprehensive image forensic analysis.
strengths:
• Fast client-side processing using Canvas API
• Effective at detecting specific AI generation artifacts
• Works with common image formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP)
• Can be combined with complementary analysis methods
• Based on established image forensics research
limitations:
• Performance may vary with image compression level
• Social media re-encoding can affect accuracy
• Best used in combination with other forensic methods
• May produce false positives on heavily processed authentic images
• Effectiveness depends on the AI generation model used

references.title: Lukas, J. et al. (2006). Digital Camera Identification from Sensor Pattern Noise. IEEE TIFS.
Chen, M. et al. (2008). Determining Image Origin and Integrity Using Sensor Noise. IEEE TIFS.
